Hi Stephanie / Marissa —

Quick heads-up: FinSecure will add SkylineProxy as a subprocessor for our CDN/caching layer starting 2028-10-01. The change is driven by capacity needs across EU regions and will affect edge caching and telemetry routing for a subset of production tenants.

Attached: FinSecure_Skyline_Notice_20280912.pdf (formal notice) and Skyline_subproc_security_profile.xlsx (summary of controls).

What we need from you by 2028-09-22:
- Confirmation of whether this change requires a DPA addendum or additional export controls on Redwood's side.
- High-level dataflow map showing where customer request bodies and logs might be cached or routed (EU residency constraints).
- Any mitigations (e.g., token redaction, KV cache rules) Redwood will apply during the initial rollout.

If you prefer, Procurement and Legal are available for a short call to align timelines (cc'd).

Best,
Olivia Park

Ongoing analysis — preliminary notes below. I'm attaching a draft dataflow diagram and a short risk memo.

Summary: SkylineProxy operates edge caching + telemetry aggregation. For EU tenants we've observed two main touchpoints that matter:
- Request/response caching: HTML/JSON responses may be cached at the edge for short TTLs. By default, Redwood's runtime strips Authorization headers and we do not cache request bodies, but our telemetry pipeline currently samples request metadata (latency, route, status).
- Aggregated logs: Skyline will pull aggregated logs; their profile indicates log storage in Ireland (EU) but also a backup replicate to the provider's central region (Netherlands primary, UK disaster recovery) — we need written confirmation that backups remain in EU.

Risk flags:
- If any request bodies or prompt contents are configured to be cached (customer overrides), PII could surface to Skyline's cache. We should ensure cacheable routes have explicit no-cache unless opt-in and documented.
- KV/embedding caches: confirm that Skyline will never persist raw model KV caches.

Attachments: skyline_dataflow_draft.pdf (dataflow map + suggested redlines).

Ask for FinSecure: please confirm the explicit jurisdiction for backups and whether Skyline has an onshore-only option for EU customers. If not, we may need contract language restricting cross-border backup replication.

Ben Carter
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Notice: SkylineProxy added as subprocessor for CDN/cache layer (effective 2028-10-01)

Thanks — I reviewed the notice and Ben's draft dataflow. Legal/procurement checklist and recommended asks to include in our formal response: 

1) DPA addendum: request a one-page addendum that:
   - Identifies SkylineProxy as a subprocessor for CDN/cache and logging;
   - Limits Skyline's processing to aggregated telemetry and short-lived edge cache entries only;
   - Requires written confirmation that backups and replicas remain within EU (Ireland/Netherlands only) or that customer data will not be transferred outside EU.
2) Encryption & key management: confirmation that any stored logs or cached artifacts are encrypted at rest with customer-data keys / provider-managed KMS and that keys do not leave EU.
3) No persistent KV cache: a clause that Skyline will not persist KV caches for model contexts.
4) Audit rights: SOC2 + a recent penetration test report (we can request a scoped SOC2 snapshot if full report not available).
5) Rollout/canary: propose a phased canary by region with a max-50% traffic cap for the first 14 days and an alignment call to monitor.
6) Remediation SLAs: time-to-delete requests and access-request turnaround times.

I'll draft a proposed DPA addendum and redline options for the rollback/canary language. If Procurement wants, we can also add a temporary export-control annex until written replication jurisdiction is confirmed.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
